Understanding educator needs to guide targeted support

The Needs Analysis is designed to identify digital teaching practices, confidence levels, resource needs, barriers and professional development priorities across the different teaching phases. The purpose is to build a clear evidence base that can guide programme planning, training and support.

Open Needs Analysis See how responses will be used

What the Needs Analysis Will Capture

The form is structured to understand both the educator's teaching context and the practical digital teaching needs that affect classroom delivery.

01

Teaching Context

School, grades taught, teaching phase and subject context so that responses can be interpreted correctly.

02

Digital Teaching Practice

Current use of devices, digital resources, assessment tools, LMS platforms, AI and interactive teaching tools.

03

Support & Development Needs

Confidence levels, barriers, training priorities and the support educators identify as most important.

Phase-Based Needs Analysis

Educators select the grades they teach and the form automatically presents the relevant phase section or sections. This allows the questions to remain appropriate to the educator's actual teaching context.

Grades 1–3

Foundation Phase

Foundational literacy and numeracy, learner engagement, basic digital skills and age-appropriate technology integration.

Grades 4–6

Intermediate Phase

Learner independence, subject integration, digital content creation, assessment and collaboration.

Grades 7–9

Senior Phase

Subject-specific digital integration, learner research, assessment, AI and preparation for the FET phase.

Grades 10–12

FET Phase

Subject-specialist teaching, CAPS alignment, examination preparation, learner performance and further-study readiness.

How Needs Analysis Responses Will Inform Decisions

Statistics generated from the Needs Analysis will help identify patterns, priorities and areas requiring intervention. The aim is to use the response data to guide targeted support instead of applying the same intervention across all educators and schools.

From response to action: Needs Analysis statistics can be examined at different programme levels so that training, resources, facilitator support and follow-up interventions can be directed to the areas where the data shows the strongest need.

Future Response Analysis Simulation Tool

A separate simulation tool is planned to support interpretation of Needs Analysis statistics. It will allow programme stakeholders to explore how different response patterns could translate into intervention priorities before or alongside live programme reporting.

Possible Intervention Classification

Green:  stronger readiness or lower intervention need
